title.narrative: Increasing Women's Resilience in Communities Impacted by Rohingya Influx

description.narrative:
The project will promote social cohesion among Rohingya and Host Community (HC) focusing on resilience building through self-reliance interventions and capacity development of the local communities. The project will target the most vulnerable people affected by conflict and disaster from the Rohingya and host communities adjacent to the camps of Ukhiya and Teknaf Upazilas. A detailed survey questionnaire will be developed based on a structured selection criteria (e.g. female-headed households, households with large numbers of family members, households with no income/livelihood source and/or heavily dependent on assistance, extremely vulnerable individuals (EVIs) like GBV referrals, person with disabilities (PwD), and households with PwD), households with minimum space for home gardening. The selected beneficiaries will be vulnerable women between 18 and 45 with 3% of persons with disabilities. The proposed project will introduce climate smart agriculture based on participants’ preferences with minimal environmental impact.
To reduce community-level tensions and strengthen community cohesion, the project will build local capacity to address and diffuse conflicts at the community level. Women will play a central role in these efforts by leading sensitization sessions and awareness-raising activities on conflict resolution, peacebuilding, gender equity, and mutual respect, promoting peaceful coexistence within communities. Inter and Intra-community dialogues, social events, and inclusive DRR sessions will contribute to mutual trust and readiness to face disaster shocks. The joint initiatives will unite members to address shared issues and reduce stigma, promoting unity and shared resilience.
This project will equip community members with portable and soft skills for future use after repatriation and will support peaceful coexistence. FIVDB will strengthen the capacity of volunteers and community representatives through training and supervision, thereby building local human resources and improving response capacity. They will share their learning with 2 nearby families, encouraging peacebuilding and resilience. These households will become indirect beneficiaries, expanding the project's community impact.
